5.13: The Hebrew has singular collective “a survivor”; BSB has plural “the survivors.”
5.14: The Hebrew names the “scribe’s staff”; BSB has “the marshal’s staff.”

5.17: The Hebrew names “seas” in the plural; BSB says “the coast” without repeating that noun.

5.22: The Hebrew repeats the galloping noun and uses singular collective “horse”; BSB has plural “horses” and says “mad galloping.”
5.24: The Hebrew uses passive blessing verbs; BSB describes Jael as “most blessed.”
5.25: The Hebrew says “a bowl of nobles”; BSB has “a magnificent bowl.”
5.26: The Hebrew explicitly names “her hand” and has plural “workers”; BSB begins with “She” and has singular “workman’s.”

5.29: The Hebrew says “wise” without an explicit superlative and names “her words”; BSB has “wisest” and leaves the words implicit in “telling herself.”
5.30: The Hebrew calls the women a “womb, two wombs” and repeatedly names the spoil; BSB says “a girl or two” and condenses the repetitions.

6.4: The Hebrew uses singular collective names for the sheep, ox, and donkey; BSB has plural “sheep,” “oxen,” and “donkeys.”
6.5: The Hebrew begins with “they”; BSB explicitly names “the Midianites.”
6.8: The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD as sender and separately says He brought them up and brought them out; BSB begins with “He” and combines the two actions into one “brought ... out.”
6.9: The Hebrew repeats singular “hand” for Egypt and all the oppressors; BSB uses plural “hands” once.
6.10: The Hebrew has singular collective “the Amorite” and explicitly names “My voice”; BSB has plural “Amorites” and “obey Me.”
6.12: The Hebrew says the angel appeared “to him”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
6.13: The Hebrew says these things “found us” and names the palm of Midian; BSB has “happened to us” and “the hand of Midian.”
6.14: The Hebrew says “this strength of yours” and uses a completed sending verb in the question; BSB has “the strength you have” and “Am I not sending you?”
6.15: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and calls the clan “my thousand”; BSB names Gideon and says “my clan.”
6.16: The Hebrew names Midian without an explicit “all”; BSB says “all the Midianites.”
6.17: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and says “in your eyes”; BSB names Gideon and says “in Your sight.”
6.18: The Hebrew leaves the second speaker unnamed; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
6.19: The Hebrew describes unleavened bread made from an ephah of flour; BSB coordinates the bread and “an ephah of flour” with “and.”
6.20: The Hebrew says “he did so”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
6.21: The Hebrew says the angel “went from his eyes”; BSB says he “vanished from his sight.”
6.22: The Hebrew repeats Gideon’s name as the speaker; BSB uses “he.”
6.25: The Hebrew refers to the person addressed as “him”; BSB names Gideon.
6.28: The Hebrew says the bull was offered on “the built altar” without an explicit word “newly”; BSB supplies “newly.”
6.29: The Hebrew repeats “this thing” in the question and answer and actively says “they said”; BSB uses “this” and “it” and the passive “they were told.”
6.30: The Hebrew repeats “because” for demolishing the altar and cutting the Asherah; BSB states the reason once for both actions.
6.31: The Hebrew ends with “because he tore down his altar”; BSB incorporates this into “with the one who has torn down his altar.”
6.32: The Hebrew actively says “he called him” without naming the caller or Gideon; BSB names Gideon and uses the passive “was called.”
6.33: The Hebrew says they crossed over without explicitly naming the Jordan; BSB supplies “the Jordan.”
6.34: The Hebrew says the Spirit “clothed” Gideon and uses a passive summoning verb for Abiezer; BSB has “came upon” and makes Gideon the one who “rallied” the Abiezrites.
6.35: The Hebrew repeats the sending of messengers twice and says Manasseh too was summoned; BSB states the sending once and combines the recipients.
6.38: The Hebrew leaves Gideon unnamed and explicitly repeats “the fleece”; BSB names Gideon and leaves the second fleece reference implicit.
6.39: The Hebrew explicitly names the fleece twice and “all the earth”; BSB uses “it” for the second fleece reference and says “the ground.”
6.40: The Hebrew explicitly says “all the earth”; BSB says “the ground.”

7.1: The Hebrew first says Jerubbaal rose early and refers to the Midianite camp as north of singular “him”; BSB combines the early rising with camping and uses plural “them.”
7.2: The Hebrew has singular “their hand”; BSB has plural “their hands.”
7.3: The Hebrew explicitly says to proclaim “in the ears” of the people; BSB says “in the hearing.”
7.4: The Hebrew repeats “with you” in both the instruction and confirmation about the man who goes; BSB omits it in the confirmation “he shall go.”
7.5: The Hebrew leaves Gideon unnamed at the start and explicitly names him in the divine speech introduction; BSB names him at the start and uses “him” in the introduction.
7.6: The Hebrew uses singular collective “their hand” and “their mouth” and explicitly says they knelt “on their knees”; BSB has plural “hands” and “mouths” and simply “knelt.”
7.7: The Hebrew says each person should go “to his place”; BSB says to “go home.”
7.8: The Hebrew begins with taking the provisions and horns and then dismissing Israel’s men; BSB places the dismissal first and makes the taking a relative clause about the three hundred.
7.9: The Hebrew says the LORD spoke “to him”; BSB explicitly names Gideon.
7.11: The Hebrew says the hands will grow strong and then to go down into the camp; BSB uses the passive “will be strengthened” and an explicit purpose “to attack the camp.”
7.12: The Hebrew calls the eastern people “sons of the east”; BSB says “all the other people of the east,” supplying “other.”
7.13: The Hebrew repeats the dream root and twice states falling, including an active overturning action; BSB has a single “dream” in the quotation and says the tent “overturned and collapsed.”
7.14: The Hebrew has both “answered” and “said”; BSB gives a single “replied.”
7.16: The Hebrew calls the companies “heads” and explicitly says the jars were empty; BSB has “companies” and “large jar,” supplying “large” and omitting “empty.”
7.17: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and repeats “so you shall do”; BSB names Gideon and uses “exactly” for the second command.
7.18: The Hebrew begins with singular “I will blow the horn”; BSB has plural “I and all ... blow our horns.”
7.19: The Hebrew says they had just raised or posted the guards; BSB describes “the changing of the guard.”
7.20: The Hebrew explicitly states the horns were held “to blow”; BSB leaves that purpose implicit in the description of holding them.
7.21: The Hebrew does not explicitly name Israelites or Midianites in this verse and separately states running, shouting, and fleeing; BSB supplies those identities and combines the enemy’s actions as fleeing while crying out and running.
7.22: The Hebrew makes each man’s sword the object God turns against his neighbor; BSB makes the men the object and says “with their swords.”
7.23: The Hebrew uses singular collective “man of Israel” and names Midian; BSB has plural “men” and “Midianites.”
7.24: The Hebrew twice names “the waters ... and the Jordan”; BSB combines them as “the waters of the Jordan.”
7.25: The Hebrew repeats the killing verb for Oreb and Zeeb and uses singular collective “head”; BSB gives the killing once for both and uses plural “heads.”

12.1: The Hebrew does not explicitly name the Jordan in the crossing and uses singular collective “man of Ephraim”; BSB supplies “the Jordan” and has plural “men.”
12.2: The Hebrew explicitly says Jephthah called “you” and has singular “their hand”; BSB says “when I called” without the object and uses plural “their hands.”
12.3: The Hebrew says Jephthah put his soul in his palm and calls the enemy “sons of Ammon”; BSB has “risked my life” and “the Ammonites.”
12.4: The Hebrew explicitly repeats Ephraim as the defeated group and calls the Gileadites “fugitives of Ephraim”; BSB uses “them” and “fugitives in Ephraim.”
12.5: The Hebrew names “Gilead” collectively and uses plural “fugitives of Ephraim”; BSB has “the Gileadites” and singular “a fugitive.”
12.6: The Hebrew says forty-two thousand “fell” from Ephraim; BSB uses the passive “were killed.”
12.7: The Hebrew explicitly repeats Jephthah’s name and calls him “the Gileadite”; BSB uses “he” and omits that designation in the death clause.
12.8: The Hebrew says “after him”; BSB explicitly names Jephthah.
12.9: The Hebrew calls the women brought in “daughters” and says he sent his own daughters “outside”; BSB has “wives” and makes marriage outside the clan explicit.
12.11: The Hebrew says “after him” and separately repeats that Elon judged Israel; BSB names Ibzan and combines the judging statements.
12.13: The Hebrew says “after him”; BSB explicitly names Elon.
12.14: The Hebrew calls the thirty descendants “sons of sons”; BSB says “grandsons.”
12.15: The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amalekite”; BSB has plural “the Amalekites.”

13.1: The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
13.2: The Hebrew says the wife had not given birth and uses a singular collective designation for the Danite; BSB says she “had no children” and uses plural “Danites.”
13.3: The Hebrew says she has not given birth; BSB says she has “no children.”
13.6: The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying” and repeats the appearance noun; BSB gives “told” and names “appearance” once.
13.8: The Hebrew asks what they should “do for” the child; BSB specifies “how to raise” him.
13.10: The Hebrew separately says she hurried, ran, told, and said; BSB combines the reporting into running quickly to tell her husband.
13.11: The Hebrew says “the woman”; BSB specifies “my wife.”
13.12: The Hebrew opens with “Now let your words come”; BSB makes this “When your words come to pass.”
13.13: The Hebrew says the woman must guard against everything spoken to her; BSB recasts this as doing everything she was told.
13.15: The Hebrew says “let us detain you” and prepare the goat “before you”; BSB has “Please stay here” and “for you.”
13.16: The Hebrew says “if you detain me” and names “your bread”; BSB has “Even if I stay” and “your food.”
13.19: The Hebrew leaves the subject of doing wonderfully unnamed; BSB explicitly names “the LORD” again.
13.20: The Hebrew repeats “the altar” with the second flame reference; BSB says simply “the flame.”
13.22: The Hebrew explicitly names Manoah and repeats the dying verb for emphasis; BSB uses “he” and “We are going to die.”
13.23: The Hebrew has singular “our hand” and says God caused them to hear this “at this time”; BSB has plural “our hands” and says “spoken to us this way.”

14.1: The Hebrew explicitly repeats Timnah’s name and calls the woman one of the Philistine daughters without an explicit word “young”; BSB names Timnah once and supplies “young.”
14.2: The Hebrew says he “went up”; BSB says he “returned.”
14.3: The Hebrew says “the daughters of your brothers” and “all my people”; BSB has “your relatives” and “any of our people.”
14.4: The Hebrew uses an unnamed “he” in the seeking clause; BSB identifies this subject as the LORD with a relative “who.”
14.5: The Hebrew uses plural “they came” for arriving at the vineyards; BSB continues with singular Samson as the subject.
14.6: The Hebrew says there was nothing in singular “his hand” and joins father and mother with “and”; BSB has “his bare hands” and “father or mother.”
14.7: The Hebrew explicitly names Samson in the pleasing clause and joins it with “and”; BSB leaves his name implicit and uses “because.”
14.8: The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the lion” with its body; BSB uses “it” for the second reference.
14.9: The Hebrew first refers to the honey with a pronoun and repeats the scooping verb later; BSB names the honey first and varies “scooped” and “taken.”
14.10: The Hebrew refers to what “young men” do in the plural; BSB describes a custom for singular “the bridegroom.”
14.11: The Hebrew leaves those who saw him unnamed; BSB supplies “the Philistines.”
14.12: The Hebrew repeats the telling verb for emphasis and separately says “and you find”; BSB combines these as “can solve it.”
14.13: The Hebrew says to tell or explain the riddle; BSB says “solve it.”
14.15: The Hebrew says “on the seventh day”; BSB says “on the fourth day.”
14.16: The Hebrew says the wife wept upon or against Samson without a separate coming verb; BSB adds that she “came to him.”
14.17: The Hebrew says he told her without an explicit noun “answer”; BSB supplies “the answer.”
14.18: The Hebrew says the men spoke “to him”; BSB explicitly names Samson.
14.19: The Hebrew leaves Samson unnamed here and ends with going up to his father’s house; BSB names him and describes the movement as returning.
14.20: The Hebrew actively describes the wife as becoming his companion’s wife without an explicit giving verb; BSB uses the passive “was given.”

19.2: The Hebrew explicitly calls her “his concubine”; BSB uses “she.” It says she went away from him, without a separate verb meaning “return.”
19.3: The Hebrew says “speak to her heart,” retaining a bodily image behind BSB’s “speak kindly to her.” It calls her father “the girl’s father,” where BSB uses “her father.”
19.4: The Hebrew has separate finite verbs for their eating, drinking, and lodging; BSB makes these activities participles.
19.5: The Hebrew says that they rose early, then that he rose to go. BSB makes the preparation to depart plural.
19.7: The Hebrew separately says that he returned and spent the night; BSB compresses this into “stayed there that night.”
19.9: The Hebrew ends with “you shall go to your tent”; BSB renders the tent as “home.”
19.10: The Hebrew repeats “with him” for the donkeys and the concubine; BSB combines them under one “with.”
19.11: The Hebrew has a separate “come, please” before “let us turn aside.” It says to lodge “in it,” referring to the city, rather than BSB’s “here.”
19.12: The Hebrew says “a foreign city” and that its inhabitants are not of the sons of Israel. BSB says “the city of foreigners” and “there are no Israelites.”
19.13: The Hebrew explicitly says that he spoke “to his servant.” It calls the destinations “places” and has no separate word corresponding to BSB’s “try.”
19.14: The Hebrew says Gibeah “which belongs to Benjamin”; BSB says “in Benjamin.”
19.15: The Hebrew leaves the subject of “he entered and sat” unnamed; BSB identifies him as “the Levite.”
19.17: The Hebrew says he “lifted his eyes”; BSB renders the bodily expression as “looked up.”
19.18: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the Levite.” It repeats Bethlehem in Judah instead of reducing the second mention to Bethlehem.
19.19: The Hebrew calls the woman “your maidservant” and describes the young man as “with your servants.” BSB says “the maidservant” and “young man with me,” then places “your servants” in the final statement.
19.20: The Hebrew says “all your need is upon me”; BSB turns the expression of responsibility into “Let me supply everything you need.”
19.22: The Hebrew describes making their heart merry and calls the attackers “sons of worthlessness.” BSB renders these expressions as “enjoying themselves” and “wicked men.” The demand literally uses “know him.”
19.23: The Hebrew says the man “came into my house”; BSB explicitly calls him “a guest.”
19.24: The Hebrew explicitly says “humble them” and “what is good in your eyes”; BSB renders these as “use them” and “as you wish.”
19.25: The Hebrew calls the man “the man,” where BSB supplies “the Levite.” It uses “knew her” for the sexual act and says he “brought her out” rather than “sent her outside.”
19.27: The Hebrew explicitly calls her “the woman, his concubine”; BSB retains only “his concubine.”
19.28: The Hebrew says he went “to his place”; BSB renders this as “for home.”
19.30: The Hebrew first says that nothing like this “has happened,” then that it “has been seen.” BSB reverses the order and uses “done” for the first expression.

20.2: The Hebrew calls the leaders “corners” of the people and describes the men as “drawing a sword.” BSB renders these as “leaders” and “armed with swords.”
20.5: The Hebrew repeats “against me” in describing their rising and surrounding the house; BSB states it once.
20.7: The Hebrew asks for “a word and counsel” here; BSB renders this as “advice and verdict” and adds “now.”
20.8: The Hebrew separately negates going to one’s tent and turning aside to one’s house. BSB combines both destinations under one return verb.
20.10: The Hebrew calls those receiving provisions “the people”; BSB identifies them as “the army.” It speaks of doing according to the outrage, where BSB explicitly says “to punish them.”
20.12: The Hebrew refers to the “tribes of Benjamin” in the plural; BSB uses the singular “tribe of Benjamin.”
20.13: The Hebrew calls the offenders “sons of worthlessness” and explicitly calls the Israelites the Benjamites’ “brothers.” BSB uses “wicked men” and “fellow Israelites.”
20.14: The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Benjamin”; BSB uses “they.”
20.15: The Hebrew says the men were counted, repeating the counting verb for the seven hundred. BSB uses “mobilized” and omits the repeated verb.
20.16: The Hebrew calls them “all this people” rather than “all these soldiers.” Its expression for left-handedness refers explicitly to the right hand.
20.17: The Hebrew says the men were counted and calls each “a man of war.” BSB uses “mobilized” and adds the qualification “experienced.”
20.19: The Hebrew says they rose “in the morning”; BSB explicitly says “the next morning.”
20.20: The Hebrew repeats “the men of Israel” as the subject of taking battle positions; BSB combines the actions under one subject.
20.21: The Hebrew says the men were destroyed “to the ground”; BSB says “on the battlefield.”
20.22: The Hebrew calls the subject “the people, the men of Israel”; BSB renders this as “the Israelite army.”
20.23: The Hebrew explicitly names “the sons of Israel” and repeats the LORD’s name three times; BSB uses “they” and replaces one occurrence with “Him.” The question uses singular “I” and “my brother,” where BSB uses plural forms.
20.25: The Hebrew explicitly says “on the second day” and “to the ground”; BSB says “that same day” and leaves the ground image implicit.
20.26: The Hebrew says “all the sons of Israel and all the people” and uses separate verbs for weeping and sitting. BSB says “the Israelites, all the people” and combines these actions as “sat weeping.”
20.28: The Hebrew’s question uses singular “I” and “my brother,” and the LORD’s answer literally commands “go up.” BSB uses “we” and “our brothers,” then renders the command as “Fight.”
20.32: The Hebrew describes them passively as “being struck before us”; BSB changes this to active “We are defeating them.”
20.34: The Hebrew leaves the subject of not knowing unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies “the Benjamites.” It describes the battle as “heavy,” rendered “fierce” in BSB.
20.35: The Hebrew describes the men as drawing a sword; BSB says they were “armed with swords.”
20.37: The Hebrew repeats “the ambush” as the subject of advancing; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “they.” Its sword expression literally says “the mouth of the sword.”
20.39: The Hebrew emphatically repeats the defeat root in the Benjamites’ statement; BSB has the single “are defeated.”
20.40: The Hebrew explicitly says that the whole city went up “toward heaven”; BSB says it went “up in smoke.”
20.41: The Hebrew uses collective singular “man of Israel” and “man of Benjamin,” with singular pronouns for Benjamin; BSB uses plural “men” and “they.”
20.45: The Hebrew leaves the pursuing subject unnamed, where BSB supplies “Israel.” It describes the taking of five thousand with a gleaning image, which BSB renders as “cut down.”
20.47: The Hebrew repeats “the rock of Rimmon” as the place where they stayed; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “where.”
20.48: The Hebrew has no separate adjective corresponding to BSB’s “other Benjamites.” It calls the cities “found,” where BSB says “in their path.”

21.1: The Hebrew uses collective singular “man of Israel” and says “to Benjamin”; BSB uses “the men of Israel” and “to a Benjamite.”
21.2: The Hebrew has singular “their voice” and repeats the weeping root in “wept a great weeping.” BSB uses plural “voices” and “weeping bitterly.”
21.3: The Hebrew introduces the speech simply with “they said”; BSB uses “they cried out.”
21.6: The Hebrew calls Benjamin “his brother” in the singular; BSB uses “their brothers, the Benjamites.”
21.10: The Hebrew describes twelve thousand “men of valor”; BSB adds the superlative “most valiant.”
21.12: The Hebrew explicitly calls the young women “virgins” and describes not knowing a man for lying with a male. BSB conveys their sexual inexperience through the relative clause alone.
21.13: The Hebrew separately says the congregation sent, spoke to the Benjamites, and proclaimed peace to them. BSB combines these actions as sending “a message of peace.”
21.14: The Hebrew actively says “they gave them the women”; BSB changes this to passive “were given the women.”
21.16: The Hebrew uses collective singular “woman” for those destroyed from Benjamin; BSB uses plural “women.”
21.17: The Hebrew names an “inheritance” for the survivors of Benjamin; BSB renders this as “heirs for the survivors.”
21.20: The Hebrew commands them to “lie in ambush” in the vineyards; BSB says “hide.”
21.21: The Hebrew repeats “the daughters of Shiloh” and uses the related expressions “dance” and “dances.” BSB retains the repeated daughters but says “perform their dances.”
21.22: The Hebrew literally asks them to “be gracious to us” concerning the women; BSB expands this to “Do us a favor by helping them.” The Hebrew leaves the daughters unnamed where BSB explicitly supplies “your daughters.”
21.23: The Hebrew explicitly says they took “wives” from the dancers whom they seized; BSB calls them “women” and describes carrying them away. The Hebrew separately says they went and returned, where BSB says “went back.”
21.24: The Hebrew separately says they departed from there and went out from there; BSB compresses this into “returned from there.”

4.1: The Hebrew places Ehud’s death after the statement about Israel’s renewed evil, joined by “and.” BSB places it first as an explicit “After” clause.
4.3: The Hebrew leaves the possessor of the chariots unnamed; BSB supplies “Jabin.”
4.6: The Hebrew introduces the divine command with the question “Has not the LORD ... commanded?” BSB uses the assertion “Surely ... is commanding.”
4.7: The Hebrew explicitly says “to you, to the torrent Kishon”; BSB retains the river destination but leaves “to you” implicit.
4.9: The Hebrew leaves the speaker of the reply unnamed until the following narrative clause; BSB identifies her as Deborah within the reply.
4.10: The Hebrew explicitly repeats Barak and Kedesh; BSB uses “he” and “where.” It says ten thousand men went up “at his feet,” rendered “followed him” in BSB.
4.11: The Hebrew names an oak at Zaanannim; BSB uses the more general “great tree.”
4.12: The Hebrew actively says “they told Sisera,” without identifying the speakers; BSB changes this to passive “Sisera was told.”
4.13: The Hebrew explicitly names Sisera; BSB uses “he.” It separately says “all his chariots” and then specifies nine hundred iron chariots, which BSB combines.
4.15: The Hebrew explicitly says “before Barak,” where BSB uses “in front of him.” It names the chariots themselves rather than BSB’s “charioteers” and says Sisera “got down from” the chariot rather than “abandoned” it.
4.16: The Hebrew’s sword expression literally says “the mouth of the sword”; BSB has “by the sword.”
4.19: The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “Sisera.” It names a milk skin rather than a general “container” and has no separate word for “again.”
4.21: The Hebrew puts Jael’s actions first and the account of his sleeping and exhaustion afterward; BSB puts the latter first as a causal circumstance. The Hebrew leaves him unnamed where BSB supplies Sisera.
4.24: The Hebrew repeats the full name and title “Jabin king of Canaan” at the end; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “him.”
